about: The lead's rulings on the Phase 1 extraction (docs/contract/extraction/*.json). Read by scripts/build-contract-docs.mjs. conflicts: keyed by the B-number of a frontend-versus-map conflict (numbered in extraction order); anything not listed is 'Proposal accepted'. answers: keyed '<feature> Q<n>'. extra: backend entries not tied to one endpoint. openQuestions: business rules put to the user, with the user's answer (answer, answeredAt); an entry without an answer uses its lead default.

11.decision: GET /health always answers 200 JSON {status: ok|degraded|down, checks} for the console; GET /health?strict=1 answers 503 when the status is down (the critical dependency, Postgres, failed) and 200 when only degraded, for load balancers (same route, so route parity holds). Decision 015.

14.decision: Accept the optional dispatch: true (change + enqueue in one transaction); the two-call flow keeps working.

16.decision: Reject on a B2C order not yet delivered runs the full refund path in the same transaction (system-approved refunds row, b2c_refund, gateway refund job). Reject on a B2C order delivered before (reopened) answers 409 USE_REFUNDS (orders Q8). Decision 025.

17.decision: Reopen reverses revenue only; cogs stays (decision 024). A later completion books cogs again only for a new supplier charge.

24.decision: Proposal accepted: the server picks the category. Created services get the create defaults of POST /admin/services (status active, fulfillment auto, price_mode fixed, duplicate_rule block_open, min_profit null, cost from the supplier item) and base_price = the suggested price (effective cost plus the default minimum profit, at least 0.02 above cost; catalog-9).

25.decision: The sync runs in the worker (supplier-sync queue); the API waits for the job up to timeout_ms + 5 s (QueueEvents) and answers its counts, or 504 SUPPLIER_TIMEOUT while the job keeps running.

32.decision: Proposal accepted, extended (lead resolution catalog-5): when the group can be deleted (no merchants, not default, not b2c_retail), in the same transaction delete its service_group_prices and the pricing_rules with group_id = id, drop the id from payment_gateways.allowed_group_ids and service_categories.allowed_group_ids, then delete the group; 204; one audit entry listing the removed rule ids. Orders keep their pricing_snapshot, so no history is lost.

35.decision: Per-kind rows; add the owner_capital equity account for opening entries (decision 024).

38.decision: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 4, 2026-10-31): manual gateways (bank, Wise: payment_gateways.is_manual) debit bank directly when staff approve; automatic gateways debit gateway_clearing until the payout moves the money to bank.

41.decision: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 3, 2026-10-31): a manual invoice is a top-up invoice: paying it posts the deposit event (the wallet is credited) and emits invoice.paid; no VAT on B2B invoices for now, the B2B VAT rate stays configurable (setting, default 0); due_at = issue + 14 days (setting).

49.decision: Proposal accepted; the side-effect GET is protected by the contract flag originCheck (Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin or same-site, or an exact CORS Origin; lead resolution b2c-8).

52.decision: Proposal accepted, restated (lead resolution b2c-13): data_requests.note exists, so the note is stored in data_requests.note and also in audit_logs.after.note; it is required (non-blank) when status = rejected.

53.decision: Proposal accepted; superseded on cost by B117 (lead resolution b2c-7): floorPrice and service.cost use the effective cost through the shared catalog pricing resolver, so cost, marginPct and floorPrice agree.

57.decision: POST /admin/content-pages/generate requires storefront:create (frontend M186); PUT /admin/risk/rules keeps the literal risk:*.

82.decision: Resolved by a console change (user decision, OPEN-QUESTIONS 7, 2026-10-31; console MISMATCHES M258): RefundStatus now has processing. The backend reports processing from approval until the gateway answers, then completed (refund.succeeded) or failed (refund.failed); a manual payout refund has no gateway step and goes straight to completed. Ledger postings follow decision 024 and scenario b2c-refund.

auth Q1.answer: Settings with defaults: staff sessions 8 h absolute, 30 min idle (last_seen_at throttled to 1/min), pre-2FA stage 10 min (decision 018).

access Q2.answer: No ROLE_PROTECTED code. One general guard instead: any change (role edit, staff role change, suspension) that would leave no active staff member holding '*' answers 409 LAST_OWNER. The Owner role can be renamed; it cannot lose '*' while it is the only source of Owners.

access Q7.answer: Yes: any action on an account whose role holds '*' requires the caller to hold '*' (403 FORBIDDEN naming '*'); closes the takeover path through a temporary password plus a 2FA reset.

audit Q8.answer: No export route: the map has none (route parity). Revisit if the map adds one.

customers Q12.answer: Refuse with 409 ERASURE_NOT_DONE until the customer is anonymized; export requests can be completed by hand.

checkouts Q3.answer: canRecover = consent AND no recovery email yet AND not paid AND older than abandonedMinutes; recovery stops 30 days after the checkout (setting); the email link starts a fresh checkout at today's price.

merchants Q7.answer: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 1, 2026-10-31): earn_threshold is USD of cumulative completed-order spend since the account was created, set per group by the admin in the console; a nightly job promotes automatically and never demotes; the admin can change a merchant's group by hand at any time. merchantCount is sent; b2c_retail is editable, never deletable or assignable; ordinary groups have kind b2b.

merchants Q13.answer: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 2, 2026-10-31, lead default accepted): lowering below the credit in use is allowed (new orders are refused until a top-up); a limit above zero on a group without overdraft_allowed is 422 on creditLimit.

finance Q6.answer: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 3, 2026-10-31): kind topup|manual|receipt|statement, status open|paid|void, invoices.description added; paying a manual invoice credits the wallet (deposit + invoice.paid); no VAT on B2B for now, the B2B VAT rate stays configurable (setting, default 0); due in 14 days (setting).

finance Q8.answer: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 4, 2026-10-31): manual gateways (bank, Wise: is_manual) debit bank directly; automatic gateways debit gateway_clearing until the payout moves it to bank.

commissions Q8.answer: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 5, 2026-10-31, lead default accepted): before approval the accrual becomes reversed (approve skips it); after approval a reversing commission entry is posted on the agent wallet.

settings Q9.answer: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 6, 2026-10-31): automatic gateways (is_manual false: card, crypto, any gateway with an API status check) credit the wallet by themselves: after the gateway confirms the payment it waits 10 minutes (setting payments.auto_credit_delay_minutes), then a job re-checks the status through the gateway API and credits the wallet only if the payment is still confirmed and risk has not flagged it (a flagged payment goes to staff review). Crypto counts as confirmed only once the gateway reports the required confirmations. Manual gateways (bank, Wise) keep staff review (approve/reject). hold_hours (whole hours, the console field) can only lengthen the wait: on an automatic gateway a value above 0 holds the payment that many hours instead of 10 minutes; on a manual gateway it is the review window after which the dashboard flags the payment.

refunds Q9.answer: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 7, 2026-10-31): the console adds processing (console MISMATCHES M258; B82 resolved); the backend returns processing between approval and the gateway result, then completed or failed.

orders Q8.answer: No: rejecting a B2C order delivered before answers 409 USE_REFUNDS; post-delivery refunds always go through /admin/refunds (refunds:approve).

services Q6.answer: User decision (OPEN-QUESTIONS 8, 2026-10-31, lead default accepted): follow the demo's resolver exactly (client price, group price, base price with the category rule, group discount, then the floor = cost + min profit); kinds margin|discount|promo, unsigned percent/fixed, rounding none|nearest_0.05|nearest_0.10|ends_99, nullable starts_at/ends_at, most specific scope wins, lowest priority within a scope. The full algorithm (scopes, window, group match, rounding step, minProfit selection) is RULES services 3.

suppliers Q7.answer: Suggested price = cost x (1 + the global margin rule), never under the floor; without a global rule the setting catalog.importDefaultMarkupPercent applies (default 60). Supplier custom fields become service_fields with supplier_key.

system-health Q2.answer: Adopt as defaults in a threshold config (code constants overridable by the settings key health.thresholds); final SLO targets stay an ops call.

access Q3.answer: CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_ROLE, LAST_OWNER (any change that would leave no active staff member holding '*': demotion, role edit, suspension), SELF_LOCKOUT (self-block, last allow rule), NOT_SUSPENDED, TWOFA_NOT_ENABLED, TWOFA_ALREADY_ENABLED. There is no ROLE_PROTECTED code (see Q2). The console shows any code's title/detail; only EMAIL_TAKEN is mapped to a field, so add errors[] with a field where a field is to blame.

services Q7.answer: Step {id, label, state, value, after, note} with value a signed fraction for category and discount, a price otherwise; ids also include the optional `rounding` step, and the label of the `category` step is dynamic (Service rule | Category rule | Global rule, by the winning rule's scope); otherGroups = every merchant group (not b2c_retail) without client override; cost = the effective cost (MISMATCHES B117), so cost + minProfit = floor; minProfit = the effective minimum profit used for the floor.

services Q2.answer: Yes. Add columns code (unique), sla_minutes, min_profit (nullable), cost_was and effective_cost (B117); compute floorPrice, marginPct and belowFloor from the effective cost; costChangedFrom = cost_was = the previous effective cost (set when a write raises the effective cost: coalesce(cost_was, old effective_cost)), cleared when a base price is saved; supplier/fallbackSupplier from links priority 1 and 2; executionMode = fulfillment with values auto|manual.

storefront Q7.answer: Yes, tac is editable (8 digits, unique) only while no IMEI check uses it (otherwise 422 on tac, catalog-7). source is manual for console entries; other writers use import or imei_check (learned from supplier check results); the console shows the raw text. marketingName is optional ('' when none). releaseYear is optional: stored null when unknown and sent as 0 (the table shows '-' for any falsy value, catalog-8).

orders Q5.answer: Superseded by MISMATCHES B92: pastSla is age-only. open (pending|processing) and placed_at older than the service SLA, with no review-queue exclusion, shared with System health; the needs_attention link of System health (M230) therefore lists those orders and keeps pastSla=true.

suppliers Q6.answer: { services, added, changed, removed, balance, balanceCheckedAt } when the supplier-sync job finishes OK; 409 SUPPLIER_DISABLED when disabled; 409 SUPPLIER_UNAVAILABLE when the job finished with a supplier failure (unreachable, refused, or the supplier call timed out inside the job); 504 SUPPLIER_TIMEOUT when the API wait (timeout_ms + 5 s, B25) ran out while the job continues; each with a readable detail.

orders Q11.answer: requested | accepted | refunded, or none (stored as NULL, sent as null as the console's string|null expects). POST /v1/orders/:id/verify and /client/orders/:id/verify set requested on a completed order within services.verify_window_h when allow_verify is true; the admin decision sets accepted or refunded.

commissions Q4.answer: Done now: commission_accruals.approved_at is set to now() in the approve transaction for each approved accrual and sent as approvedAt (ISO, null until approved) on the list and detail; the list whitelists the filters approvedAt_gte and approvedAt_lte and the sort approvedAt, so the strip can count approved accruals by approvedAt. A reversed accrual keeps status approved and approved_at.

system-health Q36.answer: ref = '<ledger_accounts.kind>:<owner_id>' for an account (client_wallet:4; bare kind for owner-less accounts); an entry finding has id = ledger_transactions.id and ref = '#<ledger_transactions.id>' (the ledger has no separate journal number); a payment finding has id = payments.id and ref = gateway_txn_id; first 20 findings per check, count = the full number. A one-account ledger filter (accountId) belongs to Finance and can be added there.

extra.decision: Schema additions (each tied to its conflict entry): sessions.stage; audit_logs.entity_label; services.code, sla_minutes, min_profit, cost_was; pricing_rules.starts_at, ends_at; staff_users.totp_last_step (a used TOTP step is never accepted twice, P2.6); inventory_codes.code_hash, code_last4; clients.suspended_at, suspended_reason, suspended_by; payments.reviewed_at, review_note; invoices.description; refunds.note; suppliers.api_key_hint (the first 5 characters of the API key, written together with api_key_enc); data_requests.note; notifications.error; webhook_deliveries.response_body, error; alert_rules.deleted_at. New values: ledger ref_type set, order_events actor types system and supplier, orders.source set, suppliers.status paused, owner_capital account.

extra.route: order placement (Dhru, REST v1, portal), supplier sync, price lists
extra.conflict: A merchant's fixed custom price stays fixed when the supplier raises its price (the Dhru behaviour a merchant pointed out). The floor used services.cost, which changes only when the admin imports changed items (M96), so orders could be sold below the new supplier cost until then.
extra.decision: User decision (2026-10-31). (1) Effective cost at order time = max(services.cost, the latest synced cost of the service's first active supplier link, credit x credit_rate in USD); floor = effective cost + minimum profit (RULES services 1); an order pays max(resolved price, floor) as before, so a fixed client or group price can no longer sell below a raised supplier cost. The supplier sync updates it at once; importing changed items stays as it is (it updates services.cost and keeps cost_was). (2) Dashboard: services_below_floor uses the effective cost, so a supplier price rise shows right after the sync. (3) Price lists show the real price: Dhru imeiservicelist/serverservicelist/fileservicelist, the REST v1 catalog, the portal catalog and the price export resolve with the effective floor; a sync that changes an effective cost bumps the catalog price version (decision 022). (4) Price-change guard on merchant orders (Dhru, REST v1, portal): the backend keeps, per merchant and service, the last price it listed to them (with currency and time; written only when it changes). If the charged price exceeds that listed price by more than the setting pricing.price_change_tolerance_percent (default 10), the order is refused: 409 PRICE_CHANGED (problem+json with listedPrice and currentPrice) or, on the Dhru surface, ERROR "Price changed. Please refresh the service list and order again.". Up to the tolerance the new price is charged and the order's pricing_snapshot records listedPrice and raised = true with the reason (floor or price change). No listing on record: no check. (5) Notifications: when the resolved price of a service changes for a merchant who placed an order for it in the last 30 days, the merchant gets one digest per change batch (service, old and new price) by email and Telegram (their notification preferences) and the outgoing webhook event service.price_changed (a backend addition to the map's three events: route parity allows it under this B-entry). (6) Lead default, not part of the user's rule: dispatch never fails over to a supplier link whose cost is above the order's charged price; such an order goes to needs_attention. This applies to automatic failover only; a staff change-supplier or dispatch may use a costlier link (recorded as costAbovePrice, resolution orders-suppliers-12). Features: 4b (resolver, listed-price memory, guard, snapshot, setting), 6 (sync recomputes the effective cost, failover check), 7a (Dhru message, listing memory on every list action), 7b (service.price_changed), 9 (dashboard alert), 12a (template and digest job).

extra.route: IP rules stage of the request pipeline
extra.conflict: The map does not say which requests an IP rule scope covers beyond admin, store and api; a broad block (scope all) would also refuse signed payment-gateway webhooks.
extra.decision: Lead decision (2026-11-01): audiences are admin (/admin), store (/store), api (/v1 and the Dhru /api/index.php) and other (/client portal, documentation and other system routes); scope all covers every audience. Incoming webhooks (/webhooks/*) and the probes /health and /metrics are never judged by IP rules: webhooks are authenticated by their signature and a block must not cost a payment (the per-IP limit and the signature check still apply).

extra.conflict: The map creates a merchant and says nothing about when its ledger accounts (client_wallet, client_hold) are opened; the first-use creation planned for feature 3 would leave a merchant without accounts and no wallet view for the 201 Client.
extra.decision: User decision (2026-11-01): the accounts are opened in the same DB transaction that creates the merchant. Feature 3 owns the public service `MerchantAccounts.open(tx, { clientId, currency: 'USD', creditLimit, overdraftAllowed })`, exported from src/modules/money/index.ts: raw inserts with ON CONFLICT (ledger_accounts_identity_uq) DO NOTHING of client_wallet (owner_type 'client', overdraft_limit = creditLimit ?? '0.0000') and client_hold (overdraft_limit 0); no postTransaction and no money event; it applies user rule 2 (creditLimit > 0 needs a group with overdraft_allowed, else 422 on creditLimit, the same answer as PATCH /admin/clients/:id/credit-limit) and returns the wallet view {balance '0.0000', reserved '0.0000', creditLimit, available}. POST /admin/clients (2a) calls it with the entered creditLimit; POST /client/auth/register (2b) calls it with creditLimit 0, so no merchant exists without accounts. 'Created on first use' stays only as a safety fallback. Order: feature 3 implements and merges first, 2a calls it; feature 3's seed creates the accounts of the demo merchants that 2a seeds. 2a reads the group (exists, kind not b2c_retail, overdraft_allowed) through a read-only ClientGroupDirectory in the catalog module's public index (4a extends it). Group moves keep the invariant: PATCH /admin/clients/:id {groupId} to a group without overdraft is 422 on groupId while the wallet's overdraft_limit is above 0, and in 4a switching a group's overdraft_allowed off is refused while any of its merchants has a limit above 0. A negative creditLimit stays 422 on creditLimit.

extra.conflict: The map says a new merchant gets a one-time sign-up token by email but not its purpose, lifetime, link or the route that consumes it.
extra.decision: auth_tokens.purpose 'invite' with subject_type 'client', a hash only, expiry 1 hour like every one-time token (decisions 010/019). The link is `<PORTAL_BASE_URL>/set-password?token=<token>`, built from the new config key PORTAL_BASE_URL (the counterpart of the console base URL). 2a writes the token and the outbox event `merchant.invited` (ids only, never the token); until feature 12a adds the template, 2b's MailSender development implementation logs a redacted line. The consuming route is POST /client/auth/password/reset {token, password}, which accepts purposes 'reset' and 'invite': it sets password_hash (argon2id), password_changed_at = now and email_verified_at = now (the link proves the email), sets used_at, voids the merchant's other unused tokens and answers 204; it does not sign in. The status stays 'pending' until staff approve with PATCH /admin/clients/:id. A merchant who misses the hour uses POST /client/auth/password/forgot, which also works for a pending merchant with no password yet. auth_tokens.purpose is a closed vocabulary: CHECK auth_tokens_purpose_check purpose IN ('invite','reset','verify_email','magic_link'), from an exported AUTH_TOKEN_PURPOSES const in src/modules/identity/db/schema.ts (STAFF_TOKEN_PURPOSES is derived from it), shipped in the lead's single pre-wave-1 audit migration (0003).

extra.conflict: No console screen calls these routes (the merchant portal is another frontend) and the map rows give only one-line descriptions. Resolution identity-platform-16 asks for per-route specs before wave 1; B122 to B136 are the specs of the 15 routes, this entry the rules they share.
extra.decision: Common rules of the merchant portal routes (ALIGNMENT § 3 and § 7, decision 018). Public routes (register, verify-email, login, password/forgot, password/reset) need no session and no CSRF token but are accepted only with an Origin header that is one of CORS_ORIGINS; pipeline order IP rules (403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED) → per-IP rate limit (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; login, 2fa and password routes have the strict limits) → handler. Session routes use the cookie gsm_client_session (httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, __Host- in production) and the readable CSRF cookie csrf_token_client; every mutation with a session sends X-CSRF-Token (403 CSRF_FAILED, never signs out); no active session is 401 UNAUTHORIZED. A sign-in creates a pending session (sessions.stage pending_totp, 10 minutes) when a second step is needed and an active one otherwise; reaching active rotates the token; lifetimes are the settings sessions.client_* (30 days absolute, 10080 minutes idle by default). Session-ending codes (401, 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED, 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED) are only ever about the caller, so a wrong current password or code is 422 on its field, never 401. Success statuses: one per route, bodies JSON or empty; lists are simple-rest. Cache-Control: no-store on /client/auth/* and on any response that carries a secret. Passwords follow the staff policy (at least 10 characters, not trivial: 422 WEAK_PASSWORD). One-time tokens (verify_email, reset, invite) are 1 hour, single use, hash only (decisions 010/019). Mails are outbox events with ids only (merchant.email_verification, merchant.password_reset, merchant.invited); 2b registers the processor that hands them to the MailSender interface. Merchant 2FA is optional TOTP (6 digits, plus or minus one step, a used step is never accepted twice: clients.totp_last_step), with clients.twofa_enabled false while the secret is only pending; the columns these specs need on clients (twofa_enabled, totp_last_step, password_changed_at) come with 2b's migration and a B116 note.

extra.conflict: No console screen calls this route (the merchant portal is another frontend); the map row only says: "Register a new merchant and send the verification email.".
extra.decision: Request {name, email (trimmed, lower-cased), password, company?, phone?, country (ISO-2, upper-cased), referralCode?}. Response 204, identical for a new and an existing email (no enumeration; comparable timing: the password hash is computed in both cases). Effects for a new email, in one transaction: insert clients with status pending, kyc_status none, the is_default group, a generated unique username and referral_code, password_hash (argon2id), referred_by_id from referralCode; MerchantAccounts.open(creditLimit 0) from feature 3 (B119); an auth_tokens row purpose verify_email (1 hour) and the outbox event merchant.email_verification. An existing email changes nothing and sends nothing. Errors: 422 VALIDATION_FAILED (errors[].field in name | email | password | country | referralCode (unknown code)), 422 WEAK_PASSWORD, 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED, 429 RATE_LIMITED.

extra.conflict: No console screen calls this route (the merchant portal is another frontend); the map row only says: "Verify the email with the token.".
extra.decision: Request {token}. Response 204; sets clients.email_verified_at = now and the token's used_at; the status stays pending until staff approve (PATCH /admin/clients/:id) and the call signs nobody in. Errors: 410 TOKEN_INVALID (unknown, expired, used or superseded token), 422 VALIDATION_FAILED on token, 429 RATE_LIMITED.

extra.conflict: No console screen calls this route (the merchant portal is another frontend); the map row only says: "Sign in; asks for a 2FA code when 2FA is enabled.".
extra.decision: Request {email, password}. Order as the staff login: IP rules → rate limit → credentials (401 UNAUTHORIZED, identical for an unknown email, a wrong password and a merchant with no password yet) → suspended (403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED) → session. A pending merchant may sign in (it can read /client/auth/me, edit the profile and, in stage 8, send KYC documents; order placement stays refused until staff approve) and an unverified email does not block sign-in. Response 200 {next: 'totp' | 'done'}: 'totp' creates a pending_totp session (10 minutes), 'done' an active one. Sets gsm_client_session and csrf_token_client and sends X-CSRF-Token. Errors: 401 UNAUTHORIZED, 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED, 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED, 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, 429 RATE_LIMITED.

extra.conflict: No console screen calls this route (the merchant portal is another frontend); the map row only says: "Complete the sign-in with a TOTP code.".
extra.decision: Request {code} (6 digits) on a pending_totp session, with CSRF. Response 204; rotates the session to active and sends X-CSRF-Token. Errors: 422 VALIDATION_FAILED on code (wrong, or a step already used), 401 UNAUTHORIZED (the pending session expired or is gone), 403 CSRF_FAILED, 429 RATE_LIMITED.

extra.conflict: No console screen calls this route (the merchant portal is another frontend); the map row only says: "Sign out and end the session.".
extra.decision: No body, with CSRF. Response 204; revokes the session and clears both cookies (Max-Age=0). A 401 counts as a successful sign-out for the portal.

extra.conflict: No console screen calls this route (the merchant portal is another frontend); the map row only says: "Send a password reset link.".
extra.decision: Request {email}. Response 204 whether or not the email is known (no enumeration, comparable timing). For an existing merchant that is not suspended, including a pending merchant who has no password yet, it creates an auth_tokens row purpose reset (1 hour) and the outbox event merchant.password_reset; the link is <PORTAL_BASE_URL>/set-password?token=<token>. Errors: 422 VALIDATION_FAILED on email, 429 RATE_LIMITED.

extra.conflict: No console screen calls this route (the merchant portal is another frontend); the map row only says: "Set a new password with the reset token.".
extra.decision: Request {token, password}; the token purpose is reset or invite (identity-platform-2). Response 204; sets password_hash (argon2id) and password_changed_at = now, sets used_at, voids the merchant's other unused tokens and revokes the merchant's sessions; with an invite token it also sets email_verified_at = now (the link proves the email); the status stays pending until staff approve. It never signs in. Errors: 410 TOKEN_INVALID, 422 WEAK_PASSWORD, 422 VALIDATION_FAILED on password or token, 429 RATE_LIMITED.

extra.decision: Response 200 Me {id, username, email, name, company, phone, country, status (pending|active|suspended), kycStatus, emailVerifiedAt (null when unverified), twofaEnabled, referralCode, group {id, name, discountPercent}, createdAt}; never password_hash, totp_secret_enc or notification_prefs secrets. extra.conflict: B34 adds ref_type payment, accrual, supplier, client and system, and B116 lists the ledger ref_type set, but the console's LedgerTransaction.refType has no 'client' word and decision 024 listed a 'ledger_transaction' type for corrections that nothing writes.
extra.decision: Lead resolution money-1, amends B34 and B116: the stored ref_type set is order, payment, invoice, refund, dispute, accrual, supplier, client, system ('ledger_transaction' is dropped). A stored 'client' (manual adjustments, ref_id = client id) is sent as refType 'system' with refId = the client id; a wire filter refType=system matches stored ref_type IN ('system','client'); every other value goes out unchanged (toWireRefType() in the money ledger read service, and the contract enum test extends to LedgerTransaction.refType). Reversals (reopen, B2B refund, b2c_refund) carry the ref of the record they reverse, never a ledger_transaction ref. ledger_transactions.ref_id is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (0 for system postings such as opening balances and gateway settlement), and postTransaction refuses 0 for any other ref_type (resolution money-6).

extra.conflict: B37 fixes the top-up statuses but the payments table also carries storefront (order) payments with their own status and method words, and map user rule 6 (gateway hold_hours) says nothing about who credits an automatic top-up.
extra.decision: Lead resolutions money-2 and money-3, user rule 6. Vocabularies per purpose: top-ups status pending|approved|rejected, method_type bank|card|usdt|wise; order payments status pending|captured|failed|refunded|partial_refund|disputed|chargeback, method_type card|wallet|crypto (CHECKs on payments). /admin/payments, /:id, /:id/approve and /:id/reject serve top-ups only (the list adds purpose='topup'; a purpose=order filter is empty; the others answer 404 for an order payment). Automatic gateways: the webhook creates the payment pending with auto_credit_at = captured_at + max(payments.auto_credit_delay_minutes 10, hold_hours); the auto-credit job posts the deposit (reviewed_by NULL, shown as reviewedBy {id: null, name: 'System'}) or sets review_required for staff; staff approve and reject are allowed only when the gateway is_manual or review_required, otherwise 409 PAYMENT_AUTO_CREDIT_PENDING (new code); job and approve share the ledger idempotency key 'deposit:payment:<id>' and a race loser gets 409 PAYMENT_ALREADY_REVIEWED. New columns payments.review_required boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false and auto_credit_at timestamptz.

extra.conflict: The console shows the payment brand in the payments report and on refunds, but payments has no such column (B116 lists the schema additions).
extra.decision: Add payments.brand text NOT NULL DEFAULT '' to the B116 schema additions (lead resolution money-4): filled by the gateway driver at capture (card '<Brand> •••• <last4>', crypto '<COIN> <network>', wallet the wallet name, top-ups '').

extra.conflict: The console sends one write-only 'secret' per gateway but the table has two encrypted columns, config_enc and webhook_secret_enc.
extra.decision: Lead resolution money-14: 'secret' is the driver's API credential and is encrypted into config_enc ({"secret": "..."}; secretHint = '••••' + last 4 characters of it). The webhook signing secret goes to webhook_secret_enc through an optional write-only body field 'webhookSecret' on POST and PATCH: a backend addition the console does not send yet (extra request fields are additive). A driver whose provider signs with the API secret reads config_enc; otherwise a missing webhook_secret_enc makes /webhooks/payments/:code answer 400 WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID. GET /admin/payment-gateways is unchanged.

The console mock still answers 409 (a mock difference, no console change). Schema: services.archived_at timestamptz NULL, CHECK services_archived_check (archived_at IS NULL OR status = 'disabled'), services_code_uq on lower(code) WHERE archived_at IS NULL, partial index services_live_type_status_idx on (type, status) WHERE archived_at IS NULL.

openQuestions.question: Which spend counts for promotion into a group, and is promotion automatic?
openQuestions.default: Cumulative completed-order spend in USD; a nightly job promotes (never demotes).
openQuestions.answer: Cumulative completed-order spend in USD since account creation; the admin sets earn_threshold per group in the console; a nightly job promotes automatically and never demotes; the admin can change a merchant's group by hand at any time.

openQuestions.question: May a credit limit be lowered below the credit already in use, and may a group without overdraft_allowed have a limit?
openQuestions.default: Lowering is allowed (new orders refused until a top-up); a limit above zero on such a group is refused (422).

openQuestions.question: What does paying a manual invoice do, and does it carry VAT?
openQuestions.default: It is a top-up: paying it credits the wallet (deposit + invoice.paid); no VAT on B2B; due in 14 days.
openQuestions.answer: Lead default accepted: paying a manual invoice credits the wallet (top-up); no VAT on B2B for now (VAT stays configurable); due in 14 days.

openQuestions.question: When staff approve a bank/Wise transfer, which account is debited?
openQuestions.default: bank for manual gateways; gateway_clearing for automatic gateways (moved to bank by payout).
openQuestions.answer: Lead default accepted: manual gateways (bank, Wise) debit bank directly; automatic gateways use gateway_clearing until payout.

openQuestions.question: What happens to a referral commission when its order is refunded or reopened?
openQuestions.default: Before approval it is reversed (not paid); after approval a reversing entry takes it back from the agent's wallet.

openQuestions.question: What does a gateway's hold_hours mean?
openQuestions.default: Hours a confirmed payment waits for manual review before the wallet is credited; nothing happens automatically when it passes, the dashboard flags it.
openQuestions.answer: Automatic gateways verified by API (card, crypto, any gateway with an API status check) wait 10 minutes after confirmation, then the wallet is credited automatically if the payment is still confirmed and not flagged by risk; crypto credits only after the gateway reports the required confirmations. Manual gateways (bank, Wise) keep manual staff review.

openQuestions.question: The map has a refund status processing that the console does not know. Change the console, or report it as completed?
openQuestions.default: Report completed once approved, failed if the gateway refund fails, until the console adds processing (preferred).
openQuestions.answer: Add processing to the console (done: console MISMATCHES M258); the backend returns processing between approval and the gateway result.

openQuestions.question: How do client prices, group prices, category/global rules, group discounts, rounding and the floor combine?
openQuestions.default: Exactly the demo's resolver: client price, else group price, else base with the category rule, then group discount, then rounding, never under the floor (cost + min profit).
openQuestions.answer: Lead default accepted. The full algorithm is RULES services 3 (lead resolution catalog-4).

openQuestions.topic: Fixed custom prices when the supplier cost rises
openQuestions.question: A merchant's custom price is fixed; when the supplier raises its price, how do we avoid selling below cost without overcharging the merchant silently? (raised by the user from a merchant conversation)
openQuestions.default: Order-time floor = cost + minimum profit on services.cost only (it changes when the admin imports the supplier's changed items).
openQuestions.answer: Floor uses max(service cost, latest synced supplier price); dashboard alert; the real price in imeiservicelist; import unchanged. An order whose price is more than a configurable tolerance (default 10%) above the merchant's last listed price is refused with PRICE_CHANGED (Dhru message: refresh the service list); within the tolerance the new price is charged and the order records the raise. Merchants who used a service in the last 30 days are notified (email, Telegram, webhook) when its price changes. Full rule: MISMATCHES B117.
